brief: A seed-starting tray of at least four cells, each with a draining bin.

requirements.requirement: Seed-starting tray of at least four cells
requirements.evidence: Four full-depth base cells in a cluster: piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0, piece:0,1,0 and piece:-1,0,0, joined by lockJoints bolts. check_build is ok with meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a draining bin
requirements.evidence: Four bin:...~hex-bin-full-drain parts, one in each of the four cells (-1,0), (0,0), (0,1), (1,0). Open faces capped with capOpenFaces so the tray has no open edges; no other issues reported.

finish.summary: Built a four-cell tray: four full-depth base cells, each holding a full-depth drained bin, joined with joint bolts and capped on open faces. The configurator reports no errors and a clear mesh check. I did not add soil or plants, since the brief only asked for the tray itself. The drainage is the bin's drilled floor; I cannot verify how well it drains or the plastic's suitability for wet soil.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
